name: Park Guell
_about: PARK GUELL, Barcelona (Antoni Gaudi, 1900-1914), on its plan (OpenStreetMap) and its ground (the IGN's 5 m terrain model): the main entrance of Eusebi Guell's garden city on the Muntanya Pelada -- the rubble wall along Carrer d'Olot with its medallions, the two gingerbread pavilions (the porter's lodge with its amanita right of the gate, the administration with its chequered hyperboloid tower and four-armed cross left of it) and the coach house, the double stair of 45 steps round the grotto, the arms and the trencadis dragon, the hypostyle room of 86 Doric columns on a 3.8 m grid under shallow white vaults and Jujol's rosettes, the Nature Square on it edged by the serpentine bench, the washerwoman's portico of leaning columns, the three viaducts on the hillside, the Casa-Museu, the Casa Larrard, and the pines. Built by tools/archgen/park_guell.py from gaudi.py's components.

hill._about: the Muntanya Pelada as the IGN's 5 m terrain model has it (MDT05), the gate's ground y 0: the vestibule levelled, the stair's cut, the hall's and the square's beds, the porticoes' galleries cut into it; let down to the world's level over the site's last 35 m (60 m behind); where it is down at the gate's level it lies just under the world's ground (the street; across the street, it is let down too)

west wall._about: the wall round the park along Carrer d'Olot (OSM 1430523773 / 1430523772), of the hill's own stone laid rough, 2-4 m over the street, holding back the gardens where they stand higher

west wall crest._about: its crest, rolled and dressed in trencadis in bands of white and red

east wall._about: the wall round the park along Carrer d'Olot (OSM 1430523773 / 1430523772), of the hill's own stone laid rough, 2-4 m over the street, holding back the gardens where they stand higher

east wall crest._about: its crest, rolled and dressed in trencadis in bands of white and red

medallions._about: the 15 medallions on the street face, 1.4 m across, 'Park' and 'Guell' in trencadis (sourced number and size; 8 m apart from the gate, estimated)

gate._about: the wrought-iron gate's two leaves (the Casa Vicens' palm leaf, set here in 1965), swung back against the pavilions' ends across the 9.1 m between them: uprights, rails, the fan of a palm leaf in each

porter's lodge._about: the porter's lodge, the Casa del Guarda (now a museum), right of the gate as one comes in (OSM 672895475): 14.80 x 7.66 m, two floors and the attic in the roof, the tower with its mirador and the amanita to 21 m

administration._about: the administration pavilion (now the shop), left of the gate (OSM 672895651): 12.60 x 6.60 m, two floors, its mushroom cupola, and at its corner by the gate the hyperboloid tower in a white and blue chequer, the cross on it at 29 m

coach house._about: the coach house behind the administration pavilion (OSM 672895744, one floor; now the bookshop), rubble, its back sunk in the rising ground

coach house crest._about: its parapet, rolled like the boundary wall's and dressed the same

landing east 1._about: the east branch's landing 1, carrying it in or out to the next flight

vestibule._about: the vestibule's paving between the stair walls' splayed ends, where the ground has risen from the gate to the stair's foot

spine 1._about: the spine's first step: the grotto's

spine 2._about: its second: the arms of Catalonia and the snake

spine 4._about: its head: the odeon's floor, level with the hall's

basins._about: the fountains' basins: the grotto's at the foot, the coat of arms' with its snake, and the one the dragon spits into

grotto._about: the first fountain: a grotto of the hill's rough stones at the spine's foot, the water welling from it into the basin

coat of arms._about: the second fountain: the four bars of the Catalan arms on the spine's face, in trencadis

snake._about: the snake's head over the arms, the water from its mouth (the serpent of Asclepius, or the Python of Delphi)

dragon bed._about: the bed of rough stone it lies on, rising behind it up the spine

dragon legs._about: its four legs, splayed out and down as a lizard's, the elbows high, the toes spread on the stone

dragon._about: El Drac, the salamander (2.4 m, sourced), in many-coloured trencadis on the third fountain: its body, the hips high on the bed, the belly low

dragon tail._about: its tail, curling round onto the stone at its side and up at the tip

dragon head._about: its head, broad and flat as a salamander's, the upper jaw lifted

dragon jaw._about: its lower jaw dropped: the open mouth the water runs from into the basin below

dragon eyes._about: its eyes, bulging on top of the head

dragon crest._about: the ridge of plates along its back, from the head to the tail

odeon bench._about: the little odeon on the stair's last landing: a curved bench facing the street, sheltered from the wind, in the sun (sourced; its size estimated)

odeon niche._about: the curved wall at the odeon's front, white trencadis framed in a band of colour: the eye the dragon lies before

stair wall west._about: the stair's side wall, close along its flights and splaying out at the foot, its face a chequer of white and coloured trencadis

planter west._about: the planter trough along the wall's top, in trencadis

stair merlons west._about: the rounded merlons along the wall's inner edge, over the stair

stair wall east._about: the stair's side wall, close along its flights and splaying out at the foot, its face a chequer of white and coloured trencadis

planter east._about: the planter trough along the wall's top, in trencadis

stair merlons east._about: the rounded merlons along the wall's inner edge, over the stair

columns._about: the hypostyle's Doric columns, 6.16 m, the plaza's rain running down inside them to a cistern

west columns._about: the west front: the outer columns inclined, feet out, along the line of the vaults' push

east columns._about: the east front: the outer columns inclined, feet out, along the line of the vaults' push

vaults._about: the ceiling: a shallow cupola over every bay, column to column, in white trencadis

rosettes._about: Jujol's four rosettes, 3 m across, where four columns were left out: suns of many points, the seasons

medallions in the vaults._about: smaller medallions, 1 m across, at the vaults' crowns: the moon's cycle

hall floor._about: the hall's floor, where the market was to be, and the terraces before its two open fronts the stair arrives on

hall walls._about: the hall's side walls and back wall, rubble, against the square's terrace and the falling ground beside it (the fronts either side of the prow are open)

square over the hall._about: the square's front over the hall: the slab on the vaults and the fill over it (its gravel drains the rain into the columns)

square._about: the Nature Square behind the hall (OSM 1105836977): the Greek theatre, the stage for the colony's fiestas, a terrace on the hill

entablature._about: the front: architrave on the outer columns, the frieze with its triglyphs, the cornice rolling out under the bench -- following the bench's waves along the hall's two fronts and its sides

gargoyles._about: lion-head gargoyles spouting the square's rain from its cornice (sourced; one every two bays, estimated)

triglyphs._about: the triglyphs on the frieze, two to a bay

bench._about: the serpentine bench along the square's edge over the hall (Gaudi and Jujol, 1910-1914; OSM 1105836969/65/70, its loops as traced): its back rolls over like a wave, its loops make little rooms; white trencadis below, every colour above
